keyQuotes: The one rule: optimise first, then commit. Every step before the Savings Plan purchase reduces what you're locking in for 1–3 years.
When every pod is over-requested by 8x, your cluster needs 8x more nodes than your workloads actually require.

Karpenter watches the actual resource requests of pending pods and provisions exactly the right EC2 instance type to satisfy them — selecting dynamically from thousands of available instance families rather than the two or three you pre-configured.
The result is a cluster that is always sized to what your workloads actually need right now, not what you anticipated at setup time.

mainPoints.explanation: The most common and expensive mistake is buying compute commitments (Savings Plans) before optimizing. This locks in waste at a discounted price for 1-3 years. The correct order is: rightsize → Karpenter → Spot → Graviton → VPC endpoints → EBS → load balancers → then commit.
mainPoints.point: Optimize before committing: always right-size requests before purchasing Savings Plans.

mainPoints.explanation: Pods are often over-requested by 8x or more. Using the Vertical Pod Autoscaler in recommendation-only mode identifies optimal requests based on actual usage. This alone reduced node count by 33% and monthly compute cost by $15,600 in the example.
mainPoints.point: Right-sizing pod resource requests using VPA is the highest-ROI first step.

mainPoints.explanation: Karpenter dynamically selects the optimal EC2 instance type for pending pods from thousands of families, consolidates underutilized nodes, and automatically falls back from Spot to On-Demand. It reduces node count by an additional 36% and cuts staging costs by 70%.
mainPoints.point: Karpenter provides intelligent bin-packing and seamless Spot fallback, outperforming Cluster Autoscaler.

mainPoints.explanation: Data transfer through NAT Gateway can account for 18% of the EKS bill. Creating Gateway and Interface endpoints for S3, DynamoDB, and ECR makes that traffic free, saving over $6,000/month in the example.
mainPoints.point: VPC endpoints eliminate NAT Gateway data transfer charges for AWS service traffic.

mainPoints.explanation: AWS Graviton ARM-based instances are 20% cheaper than equivalent x86 instances. With Karpenter managing node selection, migration is a simple nodeSelector change. Combined savings across web, data, and API workloads reached $7,600/month.
mainPoints.point: Graviton migration yields 20% cost reduction with no performance loss for most workloads.

oneSentenceSummary: A 7-step playbook to reduce EKS costs by 50-60% through rightsizing, Karpenter, Graviton migration, VPC endpoints, and more, without touching application code.
originalTitle: The EKS Cost Optimization Handbook: Reduce Your AWS Bill by 60% Using Karpenter and Rightsizing
summary: This handbook presents a proven 7-step methodology for optimizing AWS EKS costs, based on the author's experience auditing clusters at over 10 companies. It emphasizes the correct optimization sequence: right-size pod requests first, then implement Karpenter for dynamic provisioning and Spot diversification, migrate to Graviton for 20% cheaper compute, add VPC endpoints to eliminate NAT Gateway charges, optimize EBS volumes, and consolidate load balancers. Each step includes concrete commands, YAML configurations, Terraform modules, and ROI estimates. A companion GitHub repository provides ready-to-deploy scripts. The approach has consistently reduced EKS bills by 50-60%, with a case study showing a drop from $85,000/month to $34,000/month.
title: The EKS Cost Optimization Handbook: Reduce Your AWS Bill by 60% Using Karpenter and Rightsizing
